text:
rachel (Product Designer): quick design review on API Keys modal — when orgs have lots of roles the multiselect turns into a long scrollbar and users lose context that roles attach to the key not the user.

ben (PM): saw a bug report where a customer thought roles were saved on their account. tiny copy fix could help: add "These roles apply to this API key" under the picker.

omar (Frontend): reproduced keyboard issue: tabbing into the chip list sometimes traps focus and there's no clear keyboard remove action. the virtualized list also hides items.

mira (A11y): screen readers read chips as text only. things we need: an aria-live region announcing "N roles selected", labelled remove controls like "Remove role billing.read", and ensure the show-secret toggle has an accessible name + aria-pressed.

rachel (Product Designer): proposal: show up to 5 chips inline, then a "+N more" button opening a small modal with full list + checkboxes. add the one-line clarifier near picker: "These roles are granted to this API key."

ben (PM): also want a stronger inline banner when wildcard/admin scopes are selected. current yellow text is invisible to many. suggested short banner: "Warning: This key grants broad access (admin.*). Use only for trusted services." with a tiny disclosure "why" that reveals one line.

omar (Frontend): implementation notes: condensed chips can be CSS; "+N more" must be a button that opens a `role=dialog` with focus trap. i'll move arrow-key handlers to the list container to avoid traps and add labelled remove buttons for keyboard users. will add data-telemetry attributes: create_modal_open, create_submit, overflow_open, warning_ack.

mira (A11y): prefer custom disclosure toggles so we can manage `aria-expanded` and announcements. also check color contrast on the banner (small text needs stronger weight). ensure dialog gets initial focus and announces its title.

rachel (Product Designer): draft microcopy options for the banner:
- "Warning: Grants wide access (admin.*). Use only for trusted services."
- "Heads up: This key allows broad actions. Limit scopes and rotate regularly."

ben (PM): prefer the first for brevity, second for education. use disclosure rather than external docs for the small explainer.

omar (Frontend): i'll add tests for focus order and screen-reader announcements. branch name: fix/keypicker-overflow. will include `data-testid` for QA.

ci-bot: CI for branch "fix/keypicker-overflow" started — running unit + accessibility checks. link: https://ci.internal/reports/900

mira (A11y): quick QA checklist for PR:
- aria-live announces role counts on change
- remove buttons labelled and tabbable
- "+N more" button announces count and opens dialog with focus
- dialog title announced and close button labelled
- banner contrast & focus styles verified
- show-secret toggle has accessible name and `aria-pressed`

rachel (Product Designer): action items:
1) omar: implement condensed chips + overflow dialog + keyboard fixes + telemetry (PR by Thu)
2) mira: draft accessible copy & test checklist (review Wed)
3) ben: add telemetry spec + inline disclosure wording
4) rachel: update empty-state copy: "You don't have any API keys yet — create one to get started" and upload mockups for condensed chips

ben (PM): rotation follow-up: after this lands validate rotated keys keep role assignments visible in the rotate flow and show a short timeline in the modal.

omar (Frontend): noted. will make role assignments idempotent on rotate.

ci-bot: build completed for "fix/keypicker-overflow" — 2 failing accessibility tests. details: https://ci.internal/reports/900#failures

mira (A11y): i'll triage the failures (likely focus order + missing aria attributes). thanks everyone :thumbsup:
